paragraphs: Here's what I see in this one, friend. Jesus came for rest, and a crowd got there first, but He didn't send them away. Mark 6:34 says He "had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd." His plans got interrupted, and His heart went straight to the people in front of Him.

The disciples looked at a hungry crowd and saw a problem too big for them, so they wanted to send everyone away (Mark 6:35-36). Jesus looked at the same crowd and said, "You give them something to eat." (Mark 6:37) I think that stung, friend, because all they had was five loaves and two fish (Mark 6:38). But Jesus never asked them to have enough. He asked them to see what they had and put it in His hands.

So here's what I'm baking into you today. You don't have to have enough, you just have to bring what you've got and put it in Jesus' hands. He cares about hungry people, and He lets His disciples set out what He gave (Mark 6:41). Twelve basketfuls were left over (Mark 6:43), so when your own supply looks small, bring it to Him anyway.
